Step 1's diagnosis returned a NO-CHANGE verdict on ISS-0200's actual question. Read it in full at handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json -- it is your input and it is not restated here. Your job is to record that verdict and close the two gaps it exposed. You are NOT writing a result-side size rule; the diagnosis measured that there is no defect for one to target, and writing one anyway would be the failure this run exists to avoid.

ORCH has ruled on the three decisions Step 1 left open. These are routing decisions, not content decisions -- the wording is yours:

RULING 1 -- Steps 2 and 4 stay SKIPPED. Confirmed against Step 1's reasoning. Recorded in orchestrator.log, not as stub handoffs.

RULING 2 -- Step 3 is NOT empty, contrary to Step 1's reading. Three edits are required, two of them by ISS-0200's own acceptance criteria and one by core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything. Make all three.

RULING 3 -- the status-vocabulary gap is fixed in THIS run, not filed. It blocks Step 5: ISS-0200 cannot be closed without a legal terminal status, and both existing candidates assert something false. Unblock-Everything covers exactly this -- a problem that blocks completion of the current task is fixed here even when it sits outside the original scope. owned_modules is extended to docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md accordingly.

THE THREE EDITS:

(A) docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- "Issue status vocabulary". Add a terminal status for an issue that was investigated, measured, and found to carry no defect. Constraints, all load-bearing: it must NOT weaken what `resolved` asserts (a root cause was actually removed, and a regression test proves it) -- that definition exists because the registry is read as a factual record of what is still broken, and blurring it is the exact harm it guards against. It must demand the SAME evidence discipline as the other two, so it can never become the easy exit for an issue nobody investigated: say what the record must carry to earn it. State that WF-03 and this vocabulary now agree, since WF-03 Step 5 already points at this section as canonical. Name ISS-0200 as the precedent that forced it. Choose the status name yourself.

(B) docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md -- two separate places, and do not merge them:
  (i) Section 2, immediately after the existing "Why this rests on redundancy and not on brevity" block: record the result-side finding as a measured NEGATIVE result. This is the counterpart to ISS-0198's rule and belongs beside it, per ISS-0200's AC3. It MUST be unmistakably labelled as NOT a rule and as stating no threshold -- a later reader must not be able to mistake it for a size constraint on result.summary. Carry the corpus figures, the mechanisms tested and their overlap ceilings, the asymmetry argument (the dispatch defect had a duplicated copy AND an empty structured outlet; neither exists on the result side), and Step 1's own recorded method limitation -- a negative result that hides the weakness of the test that produced it is worth less than no record at all. Its purpose is that the next agent who wonders about result.summary size reads a measurement instead of re-running the investigation.
  (ii) The Enforcement note's existing "Specified but NOT YET RUNNING -- H-SIZE-1/2/3" block: extend H-SIZE-3's emit list with the result.summary figures. H-SIZE-3 is already INFO/never-fails, so this adds no gate. Add NO threshold and NO WARN -- Step 1 was explicit that a WARN here would be a length rule by the back door. The "does not run today" framing already on that block must cover the extension too.

(C) docs/issues/ISS-0191.yaml -- add the same H-SIZE-3 extension to its scope, per ISS-0200's AC5, worded so nothing implies it runs today. Keep it consistent with (B)(ii) -- these two must not drift, which is why both are in this one step.

CONSTRAINTS ON THE WHOLE EDIT:
- ISS-0200 AC4 is verifiable and will be verified by the REVIEWER gate: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement and section 2's four worked examples must come through byte-identical. Do not touch them. Run `git diff` on the file before you finish and confirm your changes are additive only.
- Do not duplicate a threshold into another file (AC3). The 6,000 WARN threshold stays where it is, mentioned in exactly one place.
- Do not edit docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml -- Step 5 owns that file.
- Section 2's JSON schema fence is declared machine-loadable and must still parse as JSON if you go near it. You should not need to.
- Commit your own edits by explicit filename. Stage docs/issues/ISS-0202.yaml too if it is still uncommitted -- ORCH wrote it and it belongs on this branch.

=== REWORK ITERATION 1 (of 3) -- ORCH, 2026-08-21T10:18:29Z ===

The closing REVIEWER gate FAILED this step on ONE BLOCKER. Read its verdict in full at handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json; the remedy is stated there per file and line and is not restated here.

READ THIS FIRST, because it changes what you are being asked to do. Almost all of your edit PASSED, including the part that was hardest to get right: ISS-0200's AC4 byte-identity was re-derived independently against merge-base 7322185 by the gate's own method and CONFIRMED, the NOT-A-RULE framing was ruled sufficient against the exact misuse it guards, the 6,000-threshold single-declaration held, (B)(ii)/(C) were called the strongest part of the edit for pointing at each other instead of duplicating, and `no_defect` was upheld on both its evidence bar and its name. Step 1's NO-CHANGE verdict also PASSED the gate on all three legs.

THIS IS A NARROW REWORK. Do not reopen any of that. Re-editing a protected span risks the byte-identity the gate just certified, and only the amended line and the paragraph it sits in will be re-gated.

(1) BLOCKER -- MANDATORY. docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:287. You wrote a statistic into a canonical protocol document that this run's OWN ISS-0202 had already measured as contaminated, two hours earlier, filed by the same agent that produced your input. The gate re-measured it independently and ruled it unsound on two separate grounds -- it is inflated (the genuine figure is 335 of 607, not 449 of 605; and only 43 of 122 in the population actually under test), and it is the wrong instrument regardless of its value, because read at face value the CORRECTED number would appear to support the very condition it is cited to refute. Apply the gate's remedy. Note what the gate also says: the clause that follows it and the attestation argument after it are sound and carry the asymmetry claim on their own, so the fix is subtraction, not replacement, unless you choose the corrected-figure-plus-qualification option.

Take the general lesson, because it is the point of this whole run: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 -- in the document you were editing -- says a re-measurement that contradicts a premise wins. Your input handoff carried a figure its own author had already contradicted in a separate artefact. Checking a number against the run's own other outputs before writing it into a canonical document is the standard here.

(2) MINOR, and ORCH rules it IN SCOPE for this rework under core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything, for the same reason Ruling 3 put ISSUE_QUEUE.md in scope: docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 hardcodes `status: resolved` in its pseudocode. An agent executing Step 5 by following it writes exactly the false status your new vocabulary entry exists to prevent -- and Step 5 of THIS run is next. It introduced no contradiction (that file correctly defers to ISSUE_QUEUE.md as canonical), so this is a catch-up, not a conflict. Two parts, per the gate: name `no_defect` as a third legal terminal value in that Step 5 block, and name in the ISSUE_QUEUE.md bullet which KEY PAIR a `no_defect` record carries -- `resolved_in_run`/`resolved_at` read wrong on a record that resolved nothing, and your bullet currently demands "the run-id and timestamp" without naming the keys. Keep that file's deference to ISSUE_QUEUE.md intact; do not restate the vocabulary there.

(3) MINOR, also in scope, same paragraph as the BLOCKER so it costs nothing extra: the gate re-derived your evidence-density figures under its own independently written metric and got the direction right but different absolute values -- and a different least-dense file than the one Step 1 named and hand-read. Those figures are now in a canonical document with the metric that produced them recorded nowhere, so they cannot be reproduced from the block and must not be read as exact. Either state the metric definition alongside the figures, or mark them explicitly as metric-dependent and directional. Your choice which; the gate did not prescribe one.

DO NOT: touch sections 2's worked examples or section 4 (AC4 protects them and the gate has certified them byte-identical); reopen the NO-CHANGE verdict; re-edit ISS-0191.yaml or the Enforcement-note extension; or fix anything else the gate raised -- the sha-recording finding is already filed as ISS-0205 (queue 205, GH#396) and is not yours to absorb.

Re-verify AC5's byte-identity claim after your edit exactly as before, and quote it: a rework is precisely when a protected span gets clipped by accident.
